test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If a X m long train running at a speed of 41 m/sec crosses a railway platform in 34 sec. Find the value of X, if the length of the railway platform is 301 m.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = Speed × Time

Total Distance = 41 × 34 = 1394 m

Length of the train (X) = Total Distance − Length of Platform

X = 1394 − 301 = 1093

**∴ The correct answer is 1093.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• Platform (301 m) Train (X m) 
• 41 m/sec 
• 
• 
• Total Distance = Speed × Time = 41 × 34 = 1394 m 
 

**Given:**

Speed of the train = 41 m/sec

Time taken to cross the platform = 34 sec

Length of the railway platform = 301 m

Length of the train = X m

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When a train crosses a platform, Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Platform

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = X + 301

⇒ X + 301 = 41 × 34

⇒ X + 301 = 1394

⇒ X = 1394 − 301

⇒ X = 1093

**∴ The correct answer is 1093.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary pole or a standing man, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train itself (Distance = Length of Train).

Train Crossing a Lengthy Object

When a train crosses a platform, a bridge, or a stationary train, the total distance covered is the sum of their lengths (Distance = Length of Train + Length of Object).

Speed Conversion Rules

To convert speed from km/hr to m/sec, multiply the speed by 5÷18. Conversely, to convert speed from m/sec to km/hr, multiply by 18÷5.
